lead.headline: Two Italian technicians are killed in a drone strike on a Rheinmetall site in Kuwait that Italy and Kuwait blame on Iran
lead.short: Two Italian technicians working for the German arms maker Rheinmetall have been killed in a strike on a facility in Kuwait, which both countries blame on Iran. Kuwait said a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani were also hurt by falling shrapnel after Iranian drones were intercepted. Iran denied responsibility, and its foreign minister called the incident "suspicious".

why.text: Attacks on Gulf states are rising again, and millions of Indians live and work in Kuwait and its neighbours.

more: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the attack looked like a "precooked recipe for war" and that Tehran would work with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause. Iran's armed forces said "no military or offensive operations have been conducted". Italy's foreign minister said investigations showed the drone was made in Iran, and that Iranian proxies were known to carry out attacks in the region.

Kuwait called it "heinous Iranian aggression" against "a vital site". It comes just over a week after Kuwait said it had repelled Iranian drone attacks on an airbase hosting US forces, the first strikes on the country in more than two months. The war began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.

update.new: A strike in Kuwait kills two Europeans.
update.front: For the first time, a strike blamed on Iran has killed European civilians in the Gulf.

seconds.headline: Zelensky calls Trump's friendship with Putin "strange", as Trump says he urged Putin to pull back from Europe
seconds.short: Volodymyr Zelensky told the BBC that Donald Trump's warm words about Vladimir Putin were "strange". "He is an aggressor, and a killer... He can't be a friend," he said, comparing it to calling Hitler a friend. Trump said on Thursday he had urged Putin, during their talks in China, to "pull back all Military aggression" in Europe.

why.text: Kyiv fears Washington is going soft on Moscow just as Ukraine waits for air-defence missiles it says are costing lives.

more: Zelensky also said delays in delivering Patriot missile systems were costing Ukrainian lives, and that the US was not putting enough pressure on Moscow. Trump had shared a picture on 21 November of himself embracing Putin and called him "my friend". Asked whether Putin was a friend of the US, Trump said: "I can't speak to America."

In his post, Trump said there was a "strong possibility" of a deal between Russia and Ukraine. "Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH," he wrote. He did not say which European territories he meant. This week Poland, a Nato member, accused Russia of deliberately violating its airspace.

facts.Trump: urged Putin to pull back in Europe

update.front: Zelensky now openly questions Trump's ties to Putin.

seconds.headline: Final New Zealand results leave Luxon's coalition one seat short, needing the centrist Opportunity party to govern
seconds.short: Final results of New Zealand's election show Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition one seat short of a majority, needing the support of Opportunity, a centrist newcomer, to stay in power or face another election. After nearly 485,000 special votes were counted, Luxon's National party dropped two seats to 40, leaving the bloc with 65 of the 130 seats.

why.text: A government hanging on one seat means a deal with a party Luxon once ruled out, or a fresh election.

more: Labour stayed on 36 seats and the Greens rose to 17. Act has 13, New Zealand First 12, Opportunity seven and Te Pāti Māori five. Labour won Wairarapa from National by just 81 votes and Hamilton East by 173, and the Greens took Wellington Bays from Labour. Preliminary results on 7 November had given the coalition a slim two-seat majority.

If National asks for a recount and wins back one seat, it could govern without Opportunity. Applications are due by 3 December, and results could take five more days. Luxon had ruled out working with Opportunity before the election but softened his stance afterwards. Special votes have historically favoured the left.

update.new: Final results cost the coalition its majority.
update.front: The final count has now taken away Luxon's majority.

seconds.headline: Bangladesh's parliament speaker says Dhaka may go to the International Court of Justice if India does not hand over Hasina
seconds.short: Bangladesh may approach the International Court of Justice if India does not extradite former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, the country's parliament speaker, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, said in Islamabad on Thursday, according to BBC Urdu. "If India does not comply, we will approach the International Court of Justice," he said, adding that Hasina would be jailed if she returned.

why.text: It turns Hasina's stay in Delhi into a legal fight that Dhaka wants to take international, and said so from Pakistan.

more: Ahmed, on a six-day visit to Pakistan, said Hasina's announcements about returning on 16 December were "just to keep her workers motivated" and that "she will not return to Bangladesh". He also said that over her 15-year rule Bangladesh had become "a colony of a neighbouring country", and that the Kashmir dispute should be settled under UN resolutions.

He claimed India had not helped Bengalis in the 1971 liberation war, only weakened Pakistan. In Dhaka, the state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, again called Hasina a "terrorist" at a briefing. On Tuesday Kobir said she could come back only in handcuffs or under strict surveillance.

stories.headline: A Thanksgiving storm cuts power to more than 900,000 US homes and businesses and postpones Macy's parade for the first time
stories.short: Storms flooded communities on the US east coast on Thursday, cutting power to more than 900,000 homes and businesses and forcing the first-ever postponement of Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade in New York, moved to Saturday over fears for its giant balloons in high winds. More than 400 flights were cancelled and 2,200 delayed, FlightAware said.

why.text: It hit the busiest travel weekend of the American year, on both coasts at once.

more: New Jersey was under a state of emergency, along with parts of New York. The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia across most of the mid-Atlantic and southern New England. In New York City, people were rescued from their cars because of flooding, said the mayor, Zohran Mamdani.

Most of the power cuts were in east coast states, according to PowerOutage.us. High winds and flooding also hit the west coast, disrupting holiday travel there. In California's Bay Area, a flood clean-up was under way after waves slammed the coastal town of Pacifica. Forecasters warned of more wind along the east coast into Friday.

stories.headline: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs for its AI push, and Swiggy's Instamart lays off 340
stories.short: SAP, Europe's most valuable software company, is preparing to cut at least 10,000 jobs, at least 9% of its workforce, to remake its business for the AI era, Bloomberg reports. In India, Swiggy's quick commerce arm Instamart has laid off about 340 people, mostly in corporate and support roles, as it adopts more AI, Moneycontrol reported.

why.text: AI is now the reason big employers give for cutting white-collar jobs, in Walldorf and in Bengaluru alike.

more: The SAP total is not final and could change after labour talks. Chief executive Christian Klein is pushing an AI-first strategy and has reorganised the board twice this year; two of its six members leave in March. All departments have been asked to find cuts, with product, engineering and sales in particular focus. SAP said it "continuously reviews its organization".

Instamart is losing money in a crowded market against Blinkit, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now. Its adjusted Ebitda loss widened to ₹895 crore in the September quarter from ₹778 crore, even as net order value grew 13.4% to ₹6,594 crore. Swiggy has not responded to the report.

stories.headline: Microsoft says Chinese and North Korean state hackers are using ARTEX, an open-source AI tool, to break into systems in hours
stories.short: Chinese and North Korean state-backed hacking groups are among those using ARTEX, an open-source AI-powered penetration testing framework, Microsoft said this week. Since its release in July, attackers have used it to automate reconnaissance, password attacks and exploitation against cloud systems, IT software and financial institutions worldwide, sometimes gaining privileged access in under three hours.

why.text: AI is making serious hacking faster and cheaper, for the most capable spy agencies and for small criminal gangs alike.

more: Users include Salt Typhoon, the Chinese group behind attacks on AT&T, Verizon, US government systems and aides to Britain's prime minister, along with Crystal Typhoon and North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. The FBI and Amazon Web Services issued warnings about the tool earlier this month.

A GitHub user called "Autumn-27" first published the code, with a Chinese-language interface, in July. The repository was taken down in October, but forks keep it in circulation in several languages, and the Chinese security company ThreatBook claimed ownership this month. Infrawatch counts more than 130 variants, making it the most widely used agentic attack framework.

stories.headline: Crystal Palace come from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1, giving Thomas Frank his first win as manager
stories.short: Crystal Palace beat Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League on Thursday after trailing to Mamadou Sarr's goal, giving Thomas Frank a first win in his first home game since succeeding Pierre Sage. The game turned 17 minutes from time when Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta, who scored the penalty. Dwight McNeil got the winner.

why.text: Palace are bottom of the Premier League, and a first win could steady them before Sunday's game against Hull.

more: McNeil made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday's defeat by Coventry. Palace had been second best for most of the night, and Yéremy Pino had a penalty saved in stoppage time before Dean Henderson made a stunning late save to seal the win and revive a European campaign that had looked lost.

"It's a season where the confidence maybe isn't the highest, to then go on and win the game is fantastic," Frank said. Palace now head into a vital league game at the bottom of the table with Hull on Sunday, with hope where there had appeared to be none.
